I1.a_publishAsync: Producer 2 (runner parent) now defines its own revPublish and revMarker. Each call takes the sample synchronously at call time, with the same keys and values as before. The file work then runs on one ordered promise chain through fs/promises: the root check (lstat, realpath, mode, uid), the target check (exists, then lstat: not a symlink, regular file, mode 0600), the 1024-byte bound, the root check again, open tmp with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW at 0600, write, filehandle.sync(), close, the root check again, then rename. Any failure sets failed and appends the marker on the same chain. A failure is sticky, so a queued sample is written as failed when an earlier write failed. The first per-case root check in revInit also moved onto that chain for producer 2.
I1.b_noReactionOnRunnerPromise: The selected control-GET observer's then() now only stops the I2 sampler. All other observer work (control validation, event 4 emit, originalPending decrement, publish, seal check) runs after setImmediate.
I1.c_cachedMode: Producer 2's send wrapper and the cut spawner's send wrapper and onMessage read one cached mode. It is refreshed by fs/promises readFile, triggered by watchFile at 25 ms. A generation counter keeps an older read from overwriting a newer one. The cut-spawner send wrapper reads the cache only for POSTs. onMessage reads it only for 'ready'.
I1.producers1and3: The shared JS for producers 1 and 3 is byte-identical to before (verified: see verification.jsByteIdentity). The producer-3 child wrappers were not changed for I1.

implementation.I2: For each selected control GET (same selection as before), a 10 ms setInterval drift sampler runs from send to settle. Each read records send-to-settle ms (ceil), the largest stall during the read (ceil, including the stretch from the last tick to settle), whether any producer-2 chain write was queued, active or started during the read, and whether any handle.kill() ran during it. The producer-2 sample carries 7 per-case keys: reads, readMaxMs, readStallMaxMs, lastReadMs, lastReadStallMs, lastReadPublishOverlap, lastReadKillOverlap. The sample key-count check was updated by +7 for producer 2 only (P10_PRODUCER2_READ_KEYS). The full per-read list goes into the R10-rev2-2 parent record. A run-level monitorEventLoopDelay histogram (10 ms resolution, spawn to exit) per child stays as context (loopDelayMaxMs, loopDelayP99Ms).
implementation.I3: In p8C6Run kinds 1 and 2, the test checks ordinary.log for run.cancel_requested source control-window for the execution. The check runs right after the terminal status and before any outcome assertion. It also runs when the terminal wait or the c6Pending wait fails. A self-stop fails the test explicitly. The failure description carries the producer-2 I2 numbers and the IPC diagnostic. No retry, no relaxed bound.
implementation.R10bMessage: A failed c6Pending wait in kinds 1 and 2 now carries: execution status, ledger state, browser_started_at SET or NULL, FINAL errorCode and errorMessage (fixed codes only; free text shows as TEXT; NOT_RECEIVED when no FINAL arrived yet), and the IPC diagnostic. The 15 s wait and the assertion are unchanged.

diagnostic_R10rev2_2.parent: Inside the existing cut-spawner spawn(), each child gets an onMessage listener that only pushes the message reference. handle.kill is wrapped: it records a fixed call-site label from the stack and keeps no frames. Labels follow the ruling enum: violation-catch, performStop-grace, other (the lead's protocol-violation and stop-grace). An onExit listener writes one line asynchronously, after setImmediate, on the producer-2 chain to TEMP/ordinary-ipc-parent.jsonl. The line holds: message kinds received (closed set), result errorCode (code pattern or OTHER), Result3 schema-valid (the runner's validateObserved with OBSERVED_LIMITS.result, run at exit, not per message), result ok, kill labels, exit code and signal, loop-delay max and p99, and the per-read I2 list.
diagnostic_R10rev2_2.child: The existing producer-3 send wrapper also keeps a reference to each outgoing message (bounded at 1024). The existing exit wrapper writes one line to TEMP/ordinary-ipc-child.jsonl: readySent, resultSent, result ok, result errorCode. This write is synchronous because process.exit never returns. It runs in the child process, not on the parent loop.
diagnostic_R10rev2_2.failedTestState: safeExecutionMetadata (failed-test-state) attaches ipcDiagnostics per execution. Java re-validates each field: numbers, booleans and closed codes only. It joins the child line by pid and execution id.
diagnostic_R10rev2_2.notCommitted: The scratch childRuntime.js in-memory load hook was not copied. No product logging change.

autoDecisions: [AUTO-DECISION] The ruling asks for every per-read number in the producer-2 sample, but the sample has a 1024-byte bound in JS and in Java, and kind 1 alone makes 44 reads → the sample carries the 7 summary keys, including the last read (the self-stop trigger read). The full per-read list goes in the parent IPC line at child exit. (Reason: no confinement bound was changed.)

[AUTO-DECISION] The child diagnostic cannot be written asynchronously at exit → it is written synchronously in the existing exit wrapper. (Reason: process.exit never returns. The write happens in the child, not the parent control path.)

[AUTO-DECISION] The kill labels use the ruling's names (violation-catch, performStop-grace, other) rather than the brief's (protocol-violation, stop-grace, other). (Reason: the ruling is the authority. The meaning is the same.)
[AUTO-DECISION] 'Publish overlapped' counts any producer-2 chain write: sample, marker or diagnostic line. (Reason: they are all instrumentation file I/O.)
